subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should OpenClaw pursue incremental session-memory indexing on the current memory_index/source-wide-batch paths, rescue the stale candidate PR, or intentionally keep full-entry reindexing for consistency?
rationale: The remaining choice affects session-state correctness, persistent memory_index schema behavior, source-wide batching, chunk-overlap semantics, and whether the open candidate branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade and real-behavior proof.

options.title: Rescue the candidate PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete schema assumptions before review continues.

options.title: Reject incremental indexing
options.body: Keep full-entry reindexing only if maintainers decide embedding cache, delta thresholds, and consistency are preferable to incremental session indexing complexity.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths with upgrade and real-behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session transcript corpus and identity work makes this the best available owner for the design choice.
